questions.question: With zero interest, a unit benefit is paid once on event $D$, where $p=P(D)$ lies in $(0,1)$, and otherwise never paid. Its ordinary quote and double-force quote both equal $p$. A student infers zero PV variance because these quotes agree. Which assessment holds for every such $p$?
options: Variance is zero because the two valuation forces agree.
Variance is positive and equals $p-p^2$.
Variance is positive and equals $p$.
Variance is negative and equals $p^2-p$.

questions.question: An insurer obtains $E[Z^2]$ for unit receipt $Z=\mathrm{e}^{-\delta\tau}\mathbf1_D$ by revaluing at force $2\delta$. Here $\tau$ is payment time and $D$ the covered event. Which part of the valuation basis must remain the same?
options: Only the payment-time law, while coverage probability is squared.
Only the covered event, while mortality rates are doubled.
The doubled financial force and a newly calibrated coverage period.
The original joint law of payment time and the covered event.

questions.question: An annual effective rate $i=-0.6$ corresponds to force $\delta=\ln(1+i)$. To obtain the second moment, a student sets the new effective rate to $2i=-1.2$. Which diagnosis follows from the valuation-rate domain?
options: Doubling $i$ makes accumulation nonpositive; doubling force remains valid.
Doubling force is invalid whenever the original effective rate is negative.
Any real negative effective rate defines a valid logarithmic interest force.
Changing mortality restores the proposed effective rate to its valid domain.

questions.question: A discounted receipt $Z$ has finite APV $E[Z]$. To use $\operatorname{Var}(Z)=E[Z^2]-(E[Z])^2$ as a finite number, which additional condition is required?
options: $E[Z^2]<\infty$
$Z$ is finite except on a probability-zero set.

questions.question: A discounted insurance receipt has APV 0.4 and second moment 0.25. What is its variance?
For a unit insurance receipt on a fixed coverage and settlement basis, PV second moment is 0.25. The benefit becomes 100 units on that same basis. What is the new PV second moment?
An insurance receipt has discounted amount 0.5 if a specified event occurs and zero otherwise. That event has probability 0.4. What is PV second moment?
Receipt X has certain PV 0.5. Receipt Y has PV 0 or 1 with equal probabilities. Both APVs are 0.5. Which variance comparison is correct?
options: Both variances are zero because both APVs are fixed at 0.5.
X has variance 0; Y has variance 0.25.
Both variances are 0.25 because both squared means are 0.25.
X has variance 0.25; Y has variance 0 because its probabilities are equal.

questions.question: A unit receipt has PV $Z=\mathrm{e}^{-\delta\tau}\mathbf1_D$, where $\tau\geq0$ is payment time, $D$ is its covered event and $\delta\geq0$ is interest force. Which second-moment comparison is guaranteed for every such model?
options: $E[Z^2]\geq E[Z]$
$E[Z^2]\leq E[Z]$

questions.question: Future lifetime $T$ is uniform on $(0,1)$ year. A benefit of $b(T)=T$ units is paid at death, with zero interest, so PV is $Z=T$. What is its variance?
An insurance unit is paid once at random time $T$ with density $f(t)=2\mathrm{e}^{-2t}$ for $t>0$. Interest force is $\delta=1$ per year, so PV is $Z=e^{-T}$ and APV is $2/3$. What is PV variance?

An original discounted benefit PV $X$ has $E[X]=2$ and $E[X^2]=5$. A new receipt has PV $Z=10+3X$, where 10 is a fixed immediate amount and 3 scales the original benefit. What is $\operatorname{Var}(Z)$?
A unit receipt is paid at time $T$ with density $f(t)=3\mathrm{e}^{-3t}$ for $t>0$. Negative interest force $\delta=-2$ gives PV $Z=\mathrm{e}^{2T}$. Which integrability conclusion is correct?
options: APV and variance are both finite because T is finite with probability one.
APV and variance are both infinite because interest is negative.
APV is finite, but the second moment is infinite, so no finite PV variance exists.
APV is finite and variance is zero because the nominal unit is fixed.

questions.question: A benefit paid at uncertain time $T\geq0$ is $b(T)=\mathrm{e}^{\delta T}$, with constant interest force $\delta>0$ and financial discount $\mathrm{e}^{-\delta T}$. Payment occurs on every outcome. An analyst says uncertain timing must give positive PV variance. Which assessment is correct?
options: The claim holds because T is random even after discounting.
The claim holds because squaring doubles discount force but leaves the benefit unsquared.
The claim fails only when the nominal benefit is constant.
The claim fails: PV equals 1 on every outcome, so variance is zero.

questions.question: A unit receipt is discounted at positive force $\delta$. Its quote at force $\delta$ is 0.8, and a purported second-moment quote at force $2\delta$ is 0.5 on the same payment-time law and event. Which audit correctly rejects this pair?
options: The second moment is below the squared mean 0.64, implying impossible negative variance.
The pair is valid because the double-force quote is smaller than the original quote.
The pair gives variance 0.14 by subtracting the second moment from squared APV.
The pair cannot be audited because two interest forces imply two different mortality laws.

questions.question: A unit receipt is paid at time $\tau=1$ or $\tau=2$ years, each with probability one half. Annual effective interest is $i=-0.2$, so annual discount factor is $v=1/(1+i)=5/4$ and PV is $Z=v^\tau$. What is its variance using the actual squared discounts?
